canonical_statement: For a geodesic segment gamma from p to q, with q not conjugate to p along gamma, the index of the second variation (index form) on endpoint-fixed variation fields equals the sum, over points gamma(t) strictly between p and q that are conjugate to p, of their conjugate-point multiplicities.
domain_and_universes: A finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold, two points p and q, and a geodesic gamma on a compact real interval; exact Lean universes and regularity classes remain to be frozen.
quantifiers: geodesic gamma from p to q
hypotheses: gamma is a geodesic segment with fixed endpoints
the terminal point q is not conjugate to p along gamma
the index form is taken on the endpoint-zero variation-field space
conclusion: index(indexForm gamma) = sum of conjugate multiplicities in the open segment

alternate_encodings.target: maximal dimension of a subspace on which the index form is negative definite
alternate_encodings.relationship: definition of the finite Morse index

alternate_encodings.target: index of gamma as a critical point of the fixed-endpoint energy functional
alternate_encodings.relationship: requires identifying the energy Hessian with the index form

excluded_degenerate_cases: The endpoint-conjugate case is excluded from this planned root because the Hessian then has nonzero nullity. Constant geodesics, boundary conjugate points, interval conventions, and infinite-dimensional completion choices require explicit later treatment.
